questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The University, UT Austin, has a excellent sociological department which offers classes not available at KU.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Interesting classes but a shame that I was not allowed to follow masters classes but only undergrad.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The overall experience was ok. Due to Covid the proces was somewhat abrupt but other than that, it was ok. I found the information provided by KU to be more obtainable than what was the case for UT Austin.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Very little, which was ok.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was just very scarce. Maybe I did not look for it very much either.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Well it was in the campus area but not on the actual campus. There are a lot of housing options around campus area. I found it optimal due to the proximity to the university and to the atmosphere you get from housing +30.000 students together within a mile or so.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I lived at Pearl Street Co-op. We were about 100 tenants or so (50% americans 50% foreigners). It was a pleasent experience. People were really nice and everybody does there very best to make the place feel comfortable. You pay a rent and on top of that there is 4 hours of work per week. That could be cooking food or taking out the trash. This makes the house run rather smoothly. 

Lunch and dinner is served monday through friday and sunday there is either brunch or dinner. Breakfast ingredients are also available. 

Once again, overall nice experience. However, I would say that the average age is quite young for a danish student. Most of the americans living there where about 20 and the other foreign students about 21. Also, the walls are crazy thin. There is quite a bit of partying going on and just generally a lot of noice being made, so if you are sensitive to that, I would really not recommend staying there.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: For undergrad courses you'll need to follow 4. The registration period is, if I am not mistaken, 2 weeks. In those three weeks you can try all the courses you like. Within that period of time, you have to decide on the 4 classes you would like to follow for the full semester and type it into the platform (cannot remember the name). Be aware that most of the time exchange students are in the bottom of the pecking order, so if a class is about to be filled up be quick and apply or find another one.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Exchange advisor. The teachers are generally very helpfull.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
Well, I wanted to register for grad school classes, which was not possible. 
However, I was able to register for all the undergrad classes I found interesting.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Contact the teachers of the class. That helps.

Additional comments:

questions.answer: a whole lot of sporting events. The football stadium, Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium, is the 9th biggest stadium in the world with more than 100.000 seats.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: the sporting events. go on trips.

questions.answer: go on trips. explore the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: rather easy. I'll never get used to the specic texan culture but general amercican cutlure is rather easy to if not adapt to then at least mimic.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: join a club (there are so many)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: the open carry law.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The hospitality.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Austin for sure is a nice city (warm most of the year) but it is rather small, so you will not get the big city vibe. Some of the faculties at the university is top class. There is a lot of both academic and non-academic activity on campus (which is very big). American students are significantly younger than Danish students.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Austin is one of the more expensive American cities.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: academic and some friendships.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Missed people at home and sometimes sleeping while a lot of noise was being made at the co-op.

questions.answer: NO
